request.spec_md:
Q1: qualifier/Q1/plain-amount.ts exports plainAmount(value, decimals, symbol) -> string. value is an integer number of base units as a string, which may start with a minus sign and may use Arabic Indic digits. The result uses Latin digits, groups thousands with commas, keeps at least 2 and at most decimals decimals (zeros beyond 2 removed from the end), writes a negative value as "minus 1,234.50 USDC" and never contains a dash. Invalid input throws.

House rules: TypeScript, tests with node:test run by tsx, each test named after the acceptance item it proves (A1, A2...), tests must fail without the change, no secrets, Latin digits only, no long dashes in any text people see.

response.notes: Implementation follows spec: digit normalization, validation, BigInt arithmetic, thousand separators, at least two decimals, trimming, negative formatting, and comprehensive tests.
